## 5. CGP AND derive-deftly own architecture and lifecycle

**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-6d72c7c9ff86207d9b.** [cgp/README.md, lines 9–15](https://github.com/contextgeneric/cgp/blob/eca0c5fda60d87cf048460f5abdd3b6e82da5e0f/README.md#L9-L15). Revision `eca0c5fda60d87cf048460f5abdd3b6e82da5e0f`; source SHA-256 `8f0eedcfac8dfdfca7d5da152b488fc48150310dc2cac074c456943854f5c8b3`.

> **A language extension for Rust, with pluggable trait implementations at compile-time.**
> 
> Context-Generic Programming (CGP) is a library on stable Rust that lifts the language's one-implementation-per-type limit off your traits: it lets one interface have many interchangeable implementations and lets each *context* — an application, a test, a deployment — plug in the one it uses. The choice is written in one readable place and resolved entirely during compilation, so it compiles down to direct calls: there is no runtime container, no reflection, and nothing left in the binary for an implementation a context does not use.
> 
> > [!IMPORTANT]
> > This repository describes **v0.8.0**, which is **not compatible** with v0.7.0 — v0.8.0 changes and removes syntax that v0.7.0 used. **All documentation in this repository describes v0.8.0 only.** For v0.7.0, refer to its published crate documentation instead.


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-bceab87ee04a464bf8.** [derive-deftly/README.md, lines 6–15](https://gitlab.torproject.org/Diziet/rust-derive-deftly/-/blob/cd9968f755c1fe8b5fba1a6d805bb79b941ed489/README.md#L6-L15). Revision `cd9968f755c1fe8b5fba1a6d805bb79b941ed489`; source SHA-256 `dca950a5170fd672562c015d6f08747335a0b7471076a083b34848f86c5861a6`.

> `derive-deftly` allows you to write macros which are driven
> by Rust data structures, just like proc macro derive macros,
> but without having to wrestle with the proc macro system.
> 
> ## Overview
> 
> You can write an ad-hoc template,
> which can speak about the fields and types in the data structure.
> You can also define named templates and apply them to multiple structures:
> effectively, you can define your own derive macro.


**Definition.** Joint ownership means one architectural cycle:

```text
source contract -> typed declaration -> derive-deftly template
 -> CGP provider implementation/delegation -> static production context
 -> CGP lifecycle consumer -> explicit effects and owned resources
```

1. CGP owns capabilities, providers, associated/context-provided types, dependency direction, runtime policy, mutable resources and child tasks. Derive-deftly owns reusable declaration-to-implementation structure, lifecycle wiring, delegation adapters and ownership metadata. Both must occur on real production paths in both projects; decorative dependencies and toy demonstrations do not count.
2. Derive-deftly operates at compile time. The generated Rust participates in runtime ownership through CGP. Do not claim that a template macro itself schedules tasks or that CGP automatically supplies application-specific lifecycle semantics.
3. Record one subsystem ownership entry: source/feature IDs; declaration and template; CGP capability/provider; production context; mutable state/resource owner; effect boundary; initialization, readiness, cancellation, drain and cleanup responsibilities.
4. Include every controller, allocator, server, SDK stream, queue, loader, pass, generator stage, publisher, background task and shutdown path. The entrypoint constructs the context and invokes the lifecycle consumer. No detached application tasks or parallel hand-maintained manager may bypass composition.
5. Preserve Agones policy for startup, retry exhaustion, lost watches, conflicts, shutdown and drain deadlines. Use Rust errors, task supervision and RAII cleanup; do not reproduce Go panic/recover or runtime behavior. Parent owners cancel and join owned children; runtime libraries supply effects through capabilities.
6. Distinguish public/wire types, portable policy and Rusternetes transport/storage types. Keep fallible conversions at the adapter boundary and preserve required unknown/optional fields. A neutral name is not architectural independence. Reusable policy consumes minimum capabilities rather than a universal orchestrator registry.
7. Reuse the existing Grafeo canonical graph/persistence owner in CPG. Borrowed views and caches are disposable projections, not independently writable graphs. Preserve source identities, numeric/encoding semantics and storage compatibility boundaries.

## 6. Pythonic readability is a coequal design requirement

**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-33a15692a6fe969ee5.** [comprende/README.md, lines 14–29](https://github.com/QuasarRay/comprende/blob/6ce005cda120f3e5ba10079f40b90dc89470b938/README.md#L14-L29). Revision `6ce005cda120f3e5ba10079f40b90dc89470b938`; source SHA-256 `248e63e8f748efe78442c56907225e1795d85dfc1fdbaa942aeaf27e06bbf6c4`.

> Comprehensions consist of a body followed by a `for ... in ...` expression,
> followed by any combination of `for ... in ...` or `if ...` expressions.
> 
> The `for ... in ...` and `if ...` expressions are nested left-to-right, so
> ```rust
> c!(do_something(x, y); for x in 0..10 if x % 2 == 1 for y in 'a'..='z');
> ```
> 
> is equivalent to:
> 
> ```rust
> for x in 0..10 {
>     if x % 2 == 1 {
>         for y in 'a'..='z' {
>             do_something(x, y);
>         }


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-f5a50c2ac98856952c.** [better-comprehension-in-rust/README.md, lines 30–46](https://github.com/Natural-selection1/better-comprehension-in-rust/blob/73ae408dff2994fef8362e34f880ff18c221045c/README.md#L30-L46). Revision `73ae408dff2994fef8362e34f880ff18c221045c`; source SHA-256 `47e4bd8dbd562d5452f801edf563546772220e1664e0708ac8531eb801da863b`.

> This library provides comprehension macros for all collection types in the Rust standard library
> 
> ( Vec and std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, BinaryHeap, HashMap, HashSet, LinkedList, VecDeque})
> 
> And provides iterator comprehension macros based on references
> 
> ## Syntax
> Value container
> ```ignore
> left_mapping <if conditions else right_mapping>?
> <for pattern in iterable <if conditions>?
> <let expression>*>+
> ```
> 
> [Key-value container](#key-value-collection-types)
> 
> Supports three key-value pair representations, which are `=>` `,` `:`


1. Evaluate authored Rust, templates, generated Rust, APIs, examples, diagnostics and later harnesses from a Python developer's viewpoint. Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust have equal standing. Both require native Rust semantics, memory safety and ownership, while preserving Agones-specific public contracts.
2. Prefer small named functions, explicit data transformations, straightforward control flow, concise comprehensions/iterators and declarative composition. Explain non-obvious borrowing, moves and error propagation beside the reusable pattern. Keep domain behavior readable without inspecting an expansion engine.
3. Use comprende's `c!` for concise mapping/filtering/collection operations; use better_comprehension when explicit collection choice, pattern/binding or lazy iteration improves clarity. Pick one convention for overlap and reuse it. Do not duplicate a transformation to exercise both libraries.
4. Use Rust-native eager/lazy evaluation, short-circuiting, ownership and allocation. Preserve Agones-required effects, duplicate handling and output ordering explicitly. A Rust HashMap does not acquire Python insertion ordering. Use an ordinary loop when an effect or cleanup sequence is clearer; record a short local reason for a non-obvious exception.
5. Keep valid Rust: explicit types, traits/generics, Option/Result and normal error propagation. No Python interpreter, dynamic object emulation, unnecessary boxing/cloning, runtime macro registry or new authoring language.
6. Preserve literal source names even where ordinary Rust spelling conventions differ. Make the registration layer explain the exception. Do not make Python familiarity an excuse to rename source files or conceal error/resource ownership.

**Worked reading pattern (schematic, not a compiled example):**

```rust
let selected = c![resource.id() for resource in &resources
                  if policy.accepts(resource)];
let decision = decide_update(&current, &desired)?;
context.apply_update(decision).await?;
```

The reader sees selection, decision and effect in order. CGP supplies the effect capability; derive-deftly supplies repeated declarations and wiring. The quoted source supplies Agones operations and domain evidence; Rust supplies language/runtime behavior.

## 7. Absolute implementation-first gate

1. Default to `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. Make ZERO attempts to test or verify any project component until all required production implementation across BOTH routes is authored and connected and every required generation output is present. A completed feature, crate, generator stage or milestone is insufficient.
2. Before the gate, prohibit Cargo check/build/test/clippy/doc/doctest, formatter/lint campaigns, rust-analyzer diagnostics, compiler/macro/API probes, fixture/smoke/example/application runs, fuzzing, benchmarks, coverage, source replay, Bolero/Kani/proofs, schema/generator validation, regeneration comparisons and CI. Do not evade this through wrappers, hooks, remote jobs or other agents.
3. Defer new semantic property extraction, harness/extraction infrastructure and assurance fixtures. Reading source tests as specifications and authoring this roadmap is permitted; executing tests or generating a property campaign is not.
4. Permitted work is source/doc reading, source-to-destination bookkeeping, necessary implementation edits, declarations/templates/rules, production configuration, local checkpoints and content identity/recovery. An already runnable generator may emit required implementation files without validation/test hooks. Its output accounting is not correctness evidence.
5. Do not compile a new generator, bootstrap project code, or run a compatibility probe under a generation label. If emission needs a forbidden build, preserve the exact dependency blocker. Do not move the output requirement behind the gate or label incomplete generation complete to escape this constraint. The cost report's finite scenarios are conditional on a permitted executable path.
6. The global gate requires every required production row, all required Agones error/edge paths using Rust-native error and ownership policy, Rusternetes integration, complete CGP/derive-deftly lifecycle wiring, production generators/support/output, and all four required metaprogramming forms in both locations. No unknown required Agones production scope, required stubs, fake success or disconnected domain operations may remain. GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED mechanisms are excluded with explicit source-bound records.
7. Record `IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE_UNVERIFIED` with contract/baseline/scope IDs, source snapshot/dirty binding, inventory revision, exact authored source/entrypoint mappings, ownership, required generated artifact identity and zero known missing required implementation. This is an authored-completeness declaration, not proof that the program is correct.
8. Only then enter `POST_IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION`, create required assurance tooling and execute deferred checks. Defects or production refactors close the gate: finish the repair, renew the global record, and resume affected checks. Harness-only corrections after the gate remain assurance work. Missing/stale/unsupported results never pass.

## 8. Complete generation and recoverable publication

1. Preserve the pipeline `CPG bundle -> normalized CPG -> typed translation IR -> Genco tokens -> generated workspace`. Persist AST/type enrichment with source/configuration identity; do not bypass CPG with an untracked Go-text emitter.
2. Preserve complete schema facts: hidden elements, inheritance, types/defaults/cardinalities, identifiers/encodings, endpoints/order, contained relationships and mutable identity. Keep standard Schema2Json behavior separate from the richer internal representation.
3. Translate every required Agones domain operation into native Rust types, control flow, errors, library calls and CGP lifecycle capabilities. Preserve source AST/types as input facts. Classify Go-only language/runtime mechanisms as superseded; do not generate a Go compatibility runtime.
4. Every required Agones operation needs a substantive implementation or real native Rust library operation with source mapping and a production consumer. Preserve independently evidenced domain failures/no-ops using Rust error policy. Retain Go-only body/operation identities with explicit supersession; declarations, comments, missing helpers and fabricated success cannot discharge Agones obligations.
5. Publish a separate complete artifact transactionally: freeze inputs; stage output and receipts; emit identity mappings and payload digests; write a completion record binding the manifest without circular self-hashing; flush/close; atomically publish the complete directory. A staged flag or multi-step copy is not publication.
6. Retain contract/source/configuration/schema/frontend/tool/dependency/rule/IR/emitter identities, exact required/emitted/missing sets, body-to-output spans, known approximations and source rights/notices. Set compilation, correctness, compatibility and production readiness to `UNVERIFIED` until later evidence establishes each category.
7. Recover intact published artifacts using minimal identity/digest bookkeeping. Preserve incomplete transactions and avoid duplicate jobs. No generation receipt alone completes the shared Goal or authorizes overwriting existing manual implementation.

## 9. Metaprogramming, assurance and delivery requirements

1. Complete `proc_macro_2`, `proc_macro_attribute_2`, `proc_macro_derive_2` and `proc_macro_delegate_2`, each supporting same-logical-crate definition/use and cross-crate export/import. Keep compiler shims/companion units internal and normal Cargo/IDE entrypoints. A stock imported macro or renamed helper crate does not satisfy local definition/use.
2. Reuse CGP, derive-deftly, existing Agones/Genco facilities, and the recorded Arcane-rs synthez/delegation/arcane patterns. Read actual pinned source for API gaps. Require a few-sentence remaining-work benefit before new generalization; no speculative framework or repeated cost investigation.
3. After the gate, demonstrate generics, visibility, aliases/re-exports, associated types/constants, async/lifecycle wiring, hygiene/diagnostics, clean/incremental rebuild and packaging where required. Preserve typed production semantics in ordinary generated Rust; never replace it under cfg(kani).
4. After the gate, preserve independent invariants for both reference models and production behavior. Agreement alone is insufficient. Retain exact examples/tables and fixture-qualified identities, then justify any generalized property with source evidence.
5. Share explicit domains/preconditions/assertions/required covers between Bolero and its Kani backend. Record exact selected harnesses, production paths, tool/compiler/backend/solver pins, bounds, unwind checks, input domains and reachable assertion/outcome witnesses. Sampling, reference proof, actual production-symbol proof, direct Kani, source replay and Rusternetes integration are separate evidence categories.
6. Preserve full source/environment/dependency closure and source-bound receipts. Empty, skipped, stale, unreachable, timed-out, unsupported, truncated or unsatisfied-cover results never count as success. Retain counterexamples and meaningful isolated negative controls. Do not weaken bounds, predicates or domains for a green result.
7. Pin application resolution and evidence toolchains; preserve immutable evidence across squash/restack. Source changes stale affected evidence; reuse genuinely unchanged obligations rather than replaying every campaign.
8. Keep local checkpoints during implementation. Avoid push/PR/merge events that would trigger forbidden checks. After eligibility, honor authorized stacked delivery into agones-rs-dev, verify exact review/merge revisions and required results, attach PRs through exposed host tools, and distinguish local, remote and visible-checkout identities. Never bypass protection or infer deployment permission from scripts.

## 10. Readability, documentation and handoff discipline

1. AGENTS.MD is the primary style reference: direct numbered obligations and concrete outcomes. Secondary book samples guide definitions, worked examples and ownership/failure explanations. They supply no new project requirements and no reason to run the commands they illustrate.
2. Preserve attribution and applicable notices for upstream excerpts and reused code. Each quote carries repository/revision/path/lines/hash; distinguish official documentation, doc comments, implementation excerpts and engineering conclusions. Dedicated prose gaps remain explicit.
3. Store only compact decisions, source mappings, status and next actions in the existing ledger; not private reasoning transcripts. Keep usage uncertainty and known blockers visible. Do not create parallel queues, a database or new background service.
4. At handoff report authored implementation, global gate, generation artifact, required assurance, delivery and cost observations separately. Report the exact next milestone and any blocked prerequisite. Document creation is not project implementation, and a forecast is not measured consumption.

# M0001 — Source mirror, version and shared contracts


**Route:** `MANUAL`. **Phase:** `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. **State:** `IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED`. **Forecast:** `F-M0001-v1` in [cost-analysis.md](cost-analysis.md).


**Prerequisites:** The shared contract and pinned source inventory.


## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-4805ffe6a2e496f31d.** [agones/site/content/en/docs/Overview/_index.md, lines 8–20](https://github.com/QuasarRay/agones/blob/6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2/site/content/en/docs/Overview/_index.md#L8-L20). Revision `6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2`; source SHA-256 `0bc9c38c2a79249df54dff3a0e11ba34db407b100cd04e7ab7d2797721f46b8a`.

> 
> _Agones, is derived from the Greek word agōn which roughly translates to “contest”, “competition at games” and “gathering”
> ([source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/agones))._
> 
> ## What is Agones?
> 
> Agones is an open source platform, for deploying, hosting, scaling, and orchestrating dedicated game servers for
> large scale multiplayer games, built on top of the industry standard, distributed system platform [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io).
> 
> Agones replaces bespoke or proprietary cluster management and game server scaling solutions with an open source solution that
> can be utilised and communally developed - so that you can focus on the important aspects of building a multiplayer game,
> rather than developing the infrastructure to support it. 


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.


## Implementation sequence


1. Establish the literal agones-rs source mirror without moving or deleting the original Go reference or existing crates. Put Cargo/module registration in rust-support/agones and use explicit path attributes for source files, including dotted filenames.

2. Carry pkg version defaults, feature-gate declarations, build/environment precedence and shared API-group constants from their exact source definitions. Connect them to explicit CGP configuration capabilities; derive-deftly owns repeated declarations and projections.

3. Record current crates as reuse candidates, with source-file and production-call-path ownership. Do not count a Rust file or previous passing test as complete parity. Keep server state and configuration owners unique.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 13 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.


**Python-familiar valid Rust example (schematic; not executed):**


```rust
use comprende::c;
use better_comprehension::vector;

let ready_names = c![server.name().to_owned()
                    for server in &servers if server.is_ready()];
let selected_ids = vector![node.id() for node in nodes.iter()
                          if node.has_required_label()];
```


These examples explain reading order and borrowing. Actual APIs must come from the selected pinned dependencies. The owning CGP provider supplies the collections; derive-deftly supplies repeated declarations/projections. Preserve Agones-required ordering and avoid redundant clones or a comprehension around complicated effects.

## Implementation sequence


1. Preserve the complete pinned CPG tree and source-relative naming. Account for Bazel helpers, sbt definitions, project helpers, launcher and protobuf/domain generation inputs; do not exclude build-only handwritten behavior.

2. Establish Rust-only Cargo/module glue outside the mirror and reuse the existing cpg-rs Grafeo-backed graph/persistence support. Record source/configuration identities and separate pristine upstream from guidance/patch overlays.

3. Author concrete Rust equivalents for required source build/tool behavior. Inspect available generator receipts without running executables. Missing runnable emission tools are explicit blockers under the strict build prohibition.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.

The complete native CPG graph/schema/build objective remains required. Preserve its functional graph, schema and interchange contracts through Rust. Go source facts may be retained for analysis/provenance; generated Agones must use the same native Rust boundary as handwritten Agones.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 49 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.

# M0003 — Errors, queues, clocks, webhooks and utility effects


**Route:** `MANUAL`. **Phase:** `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. **State:** `IMPLEMENTING`. **Forecast:** `F-M0003-v1` in [cost-analysis.md](cost-analysis.md).


**Prerequisites:** The shared contract and pinned source inventory.


## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-7a4fa54738e0818f1b.** [agones/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md, lines 9–21](https://github.com/QuasarRay/agones/blob/6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md#L9-L21). Revision `6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2`; source SHA-256 `b674bceb41ed3c9d26ca8637afc39cf67df131b785946863201f3c9bbfe41e5d`.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.


## Implementation sequence


1. Implement Agones error classes, event/log fields, readiness and CRD behavior, admission outcomes, queue retry/backoff and shutdown. Identify domain requirements from the quoted Agones utility files; source dependencies are references rather than additional Go porting objectives.

2. Use existing Rust error/formatting/logging, HTTP/TLS, serialization, filesystem notification, signal, timer and async queue/task facilities through CGP. Prefer selected native implementations and thin Agones adapters; do not reconstruct Go standard-library/runtime behavior.

3. Keep one lifecycle/resource owner and derive-deftly declarations for repeated wiring. Retire Go-only formatting/reflection/typed-nil/panic/channel/map/slice/GC/allocator/ABI gaps explicitly. Preserve unresolved Agones contracts; M0003 remains implementing until native production consumers are complete.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> // along with a stop function that can be used to unregister the signal behavior.

> }

>

## Implementation sequence


1. Account for every proto message, enum, service, streaming direction, field number, presence rule, error/status mapping and compatibility version. Treat generated .pb.go and gateway files as regeneration obligations, not disposable source.

2. Preserve alpha/beta/stable SDK boundaries, Health/WatchGameServer stream behavior, allocation messages and JSON gateway mapping. Keep protocol types distinct from Rusternetes storage objects.

3. Reuse existing Rust protocol generation and SDK types where their source mapping is known. Genco/derive-deftly own repeated bindings; retain exact source basenames such as sdk.pb.rs through explicit module registration.

4. Implement the exact API groups and versions for GameServer, GameServerSet, Fleet, FleetAutoscaler, GameServerAllocation and GameServerAllocationPolicy. Preserve metadata, selectors, resource versions, deprecated served fields and feature gates.

5. Implement Agones constructors, defaults, validation, state transitions and resource/schema support using Rust types, serde/protobuf bindings and native ownership. Preserve field presence, ranges and errors only where required by an Agones API/schema contract; never reproduce Go nil/interface or copy/runtime mechanics.

6. Assign resource lifecycle decisions to CGP providers and use derive-deftly templates for repeated resource/accessor/conversion structure. Rust public wire compatibility takes precedence over renaming fields for appearance; explain the mapping for Python readers.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 57 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

> 
> // SDKClient is the client API for SDK service.
> //
> // For semantics around ctx use and closing/ending streaming RPCs, please refer to https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/?tab=doc#ClientConn.NewStream.
> type SDKClient interface {
> 	// Call when the GameServer is ready
> 	Ready(ctx context.Context, in *Empty, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*Empty, error)
> 	// Call to self Allocation the GameServer
> 	Allocate(ctx context.Context, in *Empty, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*Empty, error)
> 	// Call when the GameServer is shutting down
> 	Shutdown(ctx context.Context, in *Empty, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*Empty, error)

> // SDKClient is the client API for SDK service.
> //
> // For semantics around ctx use and closing/ending streaming RPCs, please refer to https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/?tab=doc#ClientConn.NewStream.
> type SDKClient interface {
> 	// PlayerConnect increases the SDK’s stored player count by one, and appends this playerID to GameServer.Status.Players.IDs.
> 	//
> 	// GameServer.Status.Players.Count and GameServer.Status.Players.IDs are then set to update the player count and id list a second from now,
> 	// unless there is already an update pending, in which case the update joins that batch operation.
> 	//
> 	// PlayerConnect returns true and adds the playerID to the list of playerIDs if this playerID was not already in the
> 	// list of connected playerIDs.
> 	//
> 	// If the playerID exists within the list of connected playerIDs, PlayerConnect will return false, and the list of
> 	// connected playerIDs will be left unchanged.

> // SDKClient is the client API for SDK service.
> //
> // For semantics around ctx use and closing/ending streaming RPCs, please refer to https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/?tab=doc#ClientConn.NewStream.
> type SDKClient interface {
> 	// Gets a Counter. Returns NOT_FOUND if the Counter does not exist.
> 	GetCounter(ctx context.Context, in *GetCounterRequest, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*Counter, error)
> 	// UpdateCounter returns the updated Counter. Returns NOT_FOUND if the Counter does not exist (name cannot be updated).
> 	// Returns OUT_OF_RANGE if the Count is out of range [0,Capacity].
> 	UpdateCounter(ctx context.Context, in *UpdateCounterRequest, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*Counter, error)
> 	// Gets a List. Returns NOT_FOUND if the List does not exist.
> 	GetList(ctx context.Context, in *GetListRequest, opts ...grpc.CallOption) (*List, error)
> 	// UpdateList returns the updated List. Returns NOT_FOUND if the List does not exist (name cannot be updated).
> 	// **THIS WILL OVERWRITE ALL EXISTING LIST.VALUES WITH ANY REQUEST LIST.VALUES**
> 	// Use AddListValue() or RemoveListValue() for modifying the List.Values field.

> # Domain class generation
> 
> The Scala domain classes under `domainClasses/src/main/generated/` are generated from the schema defined in `schema/src/main/scala/io/shiftleft/codepropertygraph/schema/`. They are checked into the repository, so you only need to regenerate them when the schema changes.
> 
> Generation is handled by the `sbt-flatgraph` plugin via the `generateDomainClasses` task in the `schema` subproject. It reads `CpgSchema.instance`, which composes all schema modules, and writes Scala source files to `domainClasses/src/main/generated/`.
> 
> The task is wired as a dependency of `domainClasses/compile` and `stage`, so it runs automatically when you compile or stage:
> 
> ```
> sbt compile   # triggers generateDomainClasses, then compiles
> sbt stage     # triggers generateDomainClasses, then packages
> ```


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.


## Implementation sequence


1. Preserve SchemaBase, Base and Operators spelling and paths. Establish typed schema property/node/edge/constant handles, shared builder ownership, declaration order and source equality/identity distinctions.

2. Reconcile reusable CPGSchema and cpg-rs schema implementations at the source-declaration level. The two recorded CPG revisions have identical schema/src/main/scala blobs; this removes that text-difference concern but proves no Rust behavior or builder compatibility.

3. Use CGP providers for schema construction, native value/graph ownership and effects; derive-deftly generates repeated declaration projections. Retain signed widths, raw floating bits, UTF-16 values, nulls and scalar-list/cardinality distinctions.

4. Construct FileSystem after Base, Namespace after Base/FileSystem, and Type after Base/FileSystem. Preserve independent Configuration and MetaData declarations and exact type/property/default/cardinality definitions.

5. Retain caller-supplied builder handles and aliases; later modules may mutate earlier definitions. Do not flatten the object model into a name-only JSON map.

6. Reuse existing native module implementations by exact source path and symbols, recording unverified reuse rather than subtracting old candidate counts as if proved.

7. Construct Method after type/file/base definitions, Ast after namespace/method/type/file definitions, and CallGraph after Method/Ast.

8. Retain AST ordering, argument/parameter indices, method/type references, inheritance, contained relationships and source defaults. Preserve source module and class spellings.

9. Express module composition through CGP and repeated declarations through derive-deftly. Keep individual module APIs available; a complete factory alone does not replace them.

10. Construct Cfg, Dominators and Pdg from their already implemented Method/Ast dependencies. Preserve edge direction, endpoints, ordering, property values and layer relationships.

11. Do not equate a named graph edge with a completed analysis algorithm. Implement the actual source-owned schema behavior and keep external analysis boundaries explicit.

12. Generate repetitive typed metadata/access paths from the canonical declarations under the joint CGP/derive-deftly architecture.

13. Follow exact constructor dependencies for Shortcuts, Comment, Tags, Binding, Annotation, Finding and Hidden. Hidden is composed after its CFG/PDG/tag/shortcut dependencies.

14. Retain hidden nodes/edges/properties, duplicate declarations, inherited fields, source-specific links and mutation order. Do not use the filtered public JSON export as the complete internal schema.

15. Reuse the pinned source facts once in canonical declarations; derive API structure without dropping modules unused by Agones.

16. Implement CpgSchema, ProtoIds, ProtoSerialize and Protogen with the original names and declaration order. Compose every layer and preserve protobuf identifiers, defaults, reserved fields and options.

17. Retain build-time factories, individual parameterized APIs and mutation/equality/identity behavior. Separate immutable resolved export models from mutable source builder handles.

18. Author complete native generation inputs and provider/template wiring. Execute emission only through already available permitted generators; record unavailable fresh builds as blockers.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.

The complete native CPG graph/schema/build objective remains required. Preserve its functional graph, schema and interchange contracts through Rust. Go source facts may be retained for analysis/provenance; generated Agones must use the same native Rust boundary as handwritten Agones.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 25 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.

**Prerequisites:** [M0005](#m0005)


## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-7a4fa54738e0818f1b.** [agones/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md, lines 9–21](https://github.com/QuasarRay/agones/blob/6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md#L9-L21). Revision `6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2`; source SHA-256 `b674bceb41ed3c9d26ca8637afc39cf67df131b785946863201f3c9bbfe41e5d`.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.


## Implementation sequence


1. Regenerate the source apply-configuration family with exact resource/version/package membership. Preserve fluent builder field-presence, append/replace behavior, Agones-required presence distinctions expressed through native Rust types, metadata and extraction logic.

2. Keep each source file and dotted/generated basename in the mirror. Derive templates from canonical API declarations rather than hand-maintaining repeated field setters.

3. Make the Python-facing reading order clear: construct configuration, select fields, then submit through a CGP effect capability. Do not introduce a runtime provider registry or a second writable representation.

4. Port versioned clientset, scheme and typed-resource request construction while retaining the source package hierarchy. Preserve group/version, verb, resource, namespace, query, timeout, patch and watch behavior.

5. Bind concrete transport/storage to Rusternetes only; Kubernetes-shaped public contracts are compatibility data, not permission to add another orchestrator adapter.

6. Generate repeated forwarding with derive-deftly under CGP capabilities. Keep fake client source accounted for; any fake used solely by harnesses is deferred assurance support, never a production substitute.

7. Implement informer factories, version/resource lookup, listers and cache-index contracts with the original namespace/selector behavior and exact package/file names.

8. Preserve list/watch handoff, resync/reconnect, ordering, duplicate delivery, cache synchronization and stop behavior. The production context must not provide stronger consistency than the source contract.

9. CGP owns watch/queue scheduling, cancellation and resources; derive-deftly emits repetitive resource wiring. Keep the read snapshot separate from the unique mutable backend owner.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 88 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.

```rust
                          if node.has_required_label()];
```


These examples explain reading order and borrowing. Actual APIs must come from the selected pinned dependencies. Preserve Agones-required ordering and avoid redundant clones or a comprehension around complicated effects.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 	// MinReplicas is the minimum amount of replicas that the fleet must have

> 	// If non zero, it must be smaller than MaxReplicas and bigger than BufferSize
> 	MinReplicas *int32 `json:"minReplicas,omitempty"`

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

## Package `agones:pkg/client/clientset/versioned` -> module `pkg::client::clientset::versioned`


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-7a4fa54738e0818f1b.** [agones/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md, lines 9–21](https://github.com/QuasarRay/agones/blob/6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/high-availability-agones.md#L9-L21). Revision `6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2`; source SHA-256 `b674bceb41ed3c9d26ca8637afc39cf67df131b785946863201f3c9bbfe41e5d`.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> 
> 
> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

> ## High Availability for Agones Controller
> 
> 
> The `agones-controller` responsibility is split up into `agones-controller`, which enacts the Agones control loop, and `agones-extensions`, which acts as a service endpoint for webhooks and the allocation extension API. Splitting these responsibilities allows the `agones-extensions` pod to be **horizontally scaled**, making the Agones control plane **highly available** and more **resilient to disruption**.
> 
> Multiple `agones-controller` pods enabled, with a primary controller selected via leader election. Having multiple `agones-controller` minimizes downtime of the service from pod disruptions such as deployment updates, autoscaler evictions, and crashes.
> 
> ## Extension Pod Configurations 
> 
> The `agones-extensions` binary has a similar `helm` configuration to `agones-controller`, see [here]({{< relref "/docs/Installation/Install Agones/helm.md" >}}). If you previously overrode `agones.controller.*` settings, you may need to override the same `agones.extensions.*` setting.

## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-c29272595b076bd119.** [cpg/README.md, lines 50–61](https://github.com/ShiftLeftSecurity/codepropertygraph/blob/301c4010d28ecdac05bc2ed44310f56446459465/README.md#L50-L61). Revision `301c4010d28ecdac05bc2ed44310f56446459465`; source SHA-256 `cc3385daade4ca02a306944b7055d3c8219ed8b1a7b25f895c816647523b3d6e`.

> # Domain class generation
> 
> The Scala domain classes under `domainClasses/src/main/generated/` are generated from the schema defined in `schema/src/main/scala/io/shiftleft/codepropertygraph/schema/`. They are checked into the repository, so you only need to regenerate them when the schema changes.
> 
> Generation is handled by the `sbt-flatgraph` plugin via the `generateDomainClasses` task in the `schema` subproject. It reads `CpgSchema.instance`, which composes all schema modules, and writes Scala source files to `domainClasses/src/main/generated/`.
> 
> The task is wired as a dependency of `domainClasses/compile` and `stage`, so it runs automatically when you compile or stage:
> 
> ```
> sbt compile   # triggers generateDomainClasses, then compiles
> sbt stage     # triggers generateDomainClasses, then packages
> ```


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.

5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.

3. Post-gate milestones require the whole-project `IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLETE_UNVERIFIED` record. Run only their required assurance; if production defects reopen implementation, close and renew the gate before further checks.

4. Record the milestone outcome and actual usage observations under the separate execution/accounting policy. Follow [alternation-policy.md](#alternation-policy); this file does not define route-switch rules. Do not complete or replace the native Goal at this milestone boundary.

## Implementation sequence


1. Reuse the existing Rust SDK while accounting for first-party Go SDK behavior and public protocol compatibility. Preserve client construction, endpoints, retries, health loops, streams, errors and shutdown.

2. Keep existing language SDKs as compatibility references; this contract does not authorize wholesale rewrites of every language client. Give each retained path an explicit inventory disposition.

3. Preserve Rust SDK filenames and APIs where already compatible. Any required source-derived Go translation retains its exact Go-relative path; do not create two independently maintained canonical client semantics.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 27 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.


**Python-familiar valid Rust example (schematic; not executed):**


```rust
use comprende::c;
use better_comprehension::vector;

let ready_names = c![server.name().to_owned()
                    for server in &servers if server.is_ready()];
let selected_ids = vector![node.id() for node in nodes.iter()
                          if node.has_required_label()];
```


These examples explain reading order and borrowing. Actual APIs must come from the selected pinned dependencies. The owning CGP provider supplies the collections; derive-deftly supplies repeated declarations/projections. Preserve Agones-required ordering and avoid redundant clones or a comprehension around complicated effects.

# M0010 — Complete schema-derived domain hierarchy


**Route:** `CPG`. **Phase:** `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. **State:** `PLANNED_NOT_EXECUTED`. **Forecast:** `F-M0010-v1` in [cost-analysis.md](cost-analysis.md).


**Prerequisites:** [M0006](#m0006), [M0004](#m0004)


## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-c29272595b076bd119.** [cpg/README.md, lines 50–61](https://github.com/ShiftLeftSecurity/codepropertygraph/blob/301c4010d28ecdac05bc2ed44310f56446459465/README.md#L50-L61). Revision `301c4010d28ecdac05bc2ed44310f56446459465`; source SHA-256 `cc3385daade4ca02a306944b7055d3c8219ed8b1a7b25f895c816647523b3d6e`.

> # Domain class generation
> 
> The Scala domain classes under `domainClasses/src/main/generated/` are generated from the schema defined in `schema/src/main/scala/io/shiftleft/codepropertygraph/schema/`. They are checked into the repository, so you only need to regenerate them when the schema changes.
> 
> Generation is handled by the `sbt-flatgraph` plugin via the `generateDomainClasses` task in the `schema` subproject. It reads `CpgSchema.instance`, which composes all schema modules, and writes Scala source files to `domainClasses/src/main/generated/`.
> 
> The task is wired as a dependency of `domainClasses/compile` and `stage`, so it runs automatically when you compile or stage:
> 
> ```
> sbt compile   # triggers generateDomainClasses, then compiles
> sbt stage     # triggers generateDomainClasses, then packages
> ```


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.


## Implementation sequence


1. Regenerate every source-generated node, edge, starter, traversal, property accessor and domain class from the complete schema; never hand-port the generated Scala corpus.

2. Preserve every original generated source-relative directory and filename stem in Rust. Register case-sensitive/dotted paths explicitly in external module glue.

3. Preserve stored/detached/reference types, inheritance, defaults, cardinalities, contained-node relationships and neighbor ordering. Reuse native Grafeo ownership and projections; derive-deftly and Genco share canonical inputs with one output owner.


## Native Rust semantic boundary

1. Apply `AGONES_NATIVE_RUST_V1` and requirement 10 of the current root AGENTS.MD. Existing Rust ecosystem facilities are the default for data, errors, formatting, logging, I/O, serialization, tasks and synchronization. Custom implementation requires an identified Agones policy or concrete integration gap.
2. Record `AGONES_REQUIRED`, `RUST_NATIVE` and `GO_ONLY_SUPERSEDED` per obligation, including within mixed files. Preserve source IDs and evidence. A Go implementation mechanism does not create a runtime compatibility obligation.
3. Preserve Agones API/domain outcomes through native Rust. Do not implement Go formatting/reflection, typed-nil interfaces, panic/recover/Goexit, goroutine/channel/select behavior, map/slice internals, GC, allocator or ABI emulation. Use Rust ownership, Result/Option, RAII, existing libraries and CGP-owned tasks instead.
4. Quotes containing Go code remain source references. Source-body mappings may point to a real native Rust library operation plus the necessary Agones policy. A mapping must identify the production consumer; a label or empty wrapper is insufficient.
5. Keep CGP AND derive-deftly as joint architectural/lifecycle owners and Python-familiar valid Rust as a coequal readability requirement. The global implementation-first gate and separate alternation policy remain binding.

The complete native CPG graph/schema/build objective remains required. Preserve its functional graph, schema and interchange contracts through Rust. Go source facts may be retained for analysis/provenance; generated Agones must use the same native Rust boundary as handwritten Agones.




## Architecture, readability and authored outputs


1. Own 251 inventoried file entries in this milestone. Every required file below has a unique milestone owner.

2. Record typed declarations -> derive-deftly templates -> CGP provider implementations/delegation -> production context -> lifecycle consumer. Identify each mutable state/resource owner and effect boundary.

3. Apply Pythonic readability and idiomatic Rust as equal design criteria. Comprehensions simplify mapping/filtering; explicit small functions clarify effects. Do not add a Python interpreter, dynamic object layer, reflection registry or competing manager.

4. Preserve source-relative directories, exact case/stems and singular/plural forms. Map Go `_test.go` only to `_harness.rs`; keep Scala Test/Tests stems unchanged. Register unconventional names outside the mirror.


**Python-familiar valid Rust example (schematic; not executed):**


```rust
use comprende::c;
use better_comprehension::vector;

let ready_names = c![server.name().to_owned()
                    for server in &servers if server.is_ready()];
let selected_ids = vector![node.id() for node in nodes.iter()
                          if node.has_required_label()];
```


These examples explain reading order and borrowing. Actual APIs must come from the selected pinned dependencies. The owning CGP provider supplies the collections; derive-deftly supplies repeated declarations/projections. Preserve source ordering and avoid redundant clones or a comprehension around complicated effects.

> # Domain class generation
> 
> The Scala domain classes under `domainClasses/src/main/generated/` are generated from the schema defined in `schema/src/main/scala/io/shiftleft/codepropertygraph/schema/`. They are checked into the repository, so you only need to regenerate them when the schema changes.
> 
> Generation is handled by the `sbt-flatgraph` plugin via the `generateDomainClasses` task in the `schema` subproject. It reads `CpgSchema.instance`, which composes all schema modules, and writes Scala source files to `domainClasses/src/main/generated/`.
> 
> The task is wired as a dependency of `domainClasses/compile` and `stage`, so it runs automatically when you compile or stage:
> 
> ```
> sbt compile   # triggers generateDomainClasses, then compiles
> sbt stage     # triggers generateDomainClasses, then packages
> ```

> # Domain class generation
> 
> The Scala domain classes under `domainClasses/src/main/generated/` are generated from the schema defined in `schema/src/main/scala/io/shiftleft/codepropertygraph/schema/`. They are checked into the repository, so you only need to regenerate them when the schema changes.
> 
> Generation is handled by the `sbt-flatgraph` plugin via the `generateDomainClasses` task in the `schema` subproject. It reads `CpgSchema.instance`, which composes all schema modules, and writes Scala source files to `domainClasses/src/main/generated/`.
> 
> The task is wired as a dependency of `domainClasses/compile` and `stage`, so it runs automatically when you compile or stage:
> 
> ```
> sbt compile   # triggers generateDomainClasses, then compiles
> sbt stage     # triggers generateDomainClasses, then packages
> ```

**Route:** `MANUAL`. **Phase:** `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. **State:** `PLANNED_NOT_EXECUTED`. **Forecast:** `F-M0013-v1` in [cost-analysis.md](cost-analysis.md).

## Source contract and interpretation


**Direct quotation — UPSTREAM_DOCUMENTATION; Q-252126bb5962982bee.** [agones/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/controlling-disruption.md, lines 8–20](https://github.com/QuasarRay/agones/blob/6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2/site/content/en/docs/Advanced/controlling-disruption.md#L8-L20). Revision `6eb4a02588d8e7b581de187f3bc849733a78dcb2`; source SHA-256 `e099ae789c0faba275ee0f35b86a6fa0f646a81b62879e139c47d9ee8c300ee9`.

> 
> ## Disruption in Kubernetes
> 
> [A `Pod` in Kubernetes may be disrupted](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/disruptions/#voluntary-and-involuntary-disruptions) for involuntary reasons, e.g. hardware failure, or voluntary reasons, such as when nodes are drained for upgrades. 
> 
> By default, Agones assumes your game server should never be disrupted voluntarily and configures the `Pod` appropriately - but this isn't always the ideal setting. Here we discuss how Agones allows you to control the two most significant sources of voluntary `Pod` evictions, node upgrades and Cluster Autoscaler, using the `eviction` API on the `GameServer` object. 
> 
> ## Benefits of Allowing Voluntary Disruption
> 
> It's not always easy to write your game server in a way that allows for disruption, but it can have major benefits:
> 
> * Compaction of your cluster using [Cluster Autoscaler](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/tree/master/cluster-autoscaler) can lead to considerable cost savings for your infrastructure.
> * Allowing automated node upgrades can save you management toil, and lowers the time it takes to patch security vulnerabilites.


**Derived instruction.** Implement the source obligations below through the shared CGP AND derive-deftly architecture. Direct quotations are reference data; this roadmap’s user-authorized phase and integration constraints govern execution.

> 		case agonesv1.EvictionSafeOnUpgrade, agonesv1.EvictionSafeNever:

> 			// (on Autopilot, this enables Extended Duration pods, which is equivalent).

> /** Mutable data structure to preserve mapping between proto and cpg nodes during ProtoToCpg import.
>   *
>   * Context: we need to run two passes: 1) add nodes and 2) set node properties and add edges (this is due to
>   * flatgraph-specific implementation details)

>   * Because of that, we need to remember the mapping from proto node id to gnode. Typically, that's just a plain
>   * mapping. But there's one special case for TYPE nodes: some (parallel) frontends create duplicate TYPE nodes which we
>   * need to deduplicate...
>   */
> class ProtoToGraphNodeMappings {
>   private val protoNodeIdToGNode  = mutable.LongMap.empty[DNode]
>   private val typeFullNameToGNode = mutable.Map.empty[String, DNode]
> 
>   def add(protoNode: CpgStruct.Node, node: DNode): Unit = {
>     protoNodeIdToGNode += protoNode.getKey -> node
>     typeFullNameMaybe(protoNode).foreach(typeFullName => typeFullNameToGNode += typeFullName -> node)
>   }

**Route:** `MANUAL`. **Phase:** `IMPLEMENTATION_ONLY`. **State:** `PLANNED_NOT_EXECUTED`. **Forecast:** `F-M0017-v1` in [cost-analysis.md](cost-analysis.md).
